answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Mass identity fraud is economically unattractive here, not because it is caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale. It is like tending a zenith garden, watching a jade bird settle, and feeling the calm of a gale at dusk — slow trust, instantly lost.
